headline: Running Out of Room? Key Questions for a Home Addition
articleBody:
Does your home feel like it's shrinking? As your family or lifestyle changes, you might find yourself needing more space. A room addition is a fantastic way to get the square footage you need without moving, but it's a major project with a lot of moving parts. Knowing the right questions to ask is the first step.

The initial big decision is whether to build out or build up. This often depends on local zoning rules which limit how much of your lot you can cover. A professional can help you figure out what's feasible. Next, consider how the new structure will integrate with your existing home. You want it to look seamless, not like a box that was just tacked on. This involves complex work to tie into the foundation and match the roofline, siding, and windows. Don't forget about your home's systems. Your current HVAC and electrical panel might not be able to handle the extra load of a new room, so upgrades may be necessary. Finally, remember that almost every room addition requires a full set of permits and inspections.
